title: Palindrome Pairs
summary: Given an array of unique strings, find all pairs of indices (i, j) where concatenating the strings at these indices results in a palindrome, and i ≠ j.
statement: Given an array of unique strings, find all pairs of indices (i, j) where concatenating the strings at these indices results in a palindrome, and i ≠ j. Return these pairs.
constraints: 1 <= len(words) <= 5000; all words are distinct; each has 0–300 lowercase English letters.

Return every ordered pair [i,j] with i != j such that words[i]+words[j] is a palindrome. Pair order in the answer is arbitrary; the two orders of indices are separate answers. An empty word is allowed.
Target linear work in total input characters plus produced pairs; avoid checking every possible word pair or rescanning every substring for palindromes.
target_time_complexity: O(S+w+p), input characters S, word count w, output pairs p
hints: A shorter word can match the reverse of part of a longer word when the unmatched part is a palindrome.
Insert reversed words into a trie. At each node remember which words have a palindromic prefix still unconsumed.
While querying a word, an earlier terminal matches if the remaining suffix is palindromic. After consuming the word, emit stored palindromic remainders. Exclude the same index.
Precompute all palindromic prefix/suffix lengths in linear time using KMP on text+# + reversed(text), following its failure-link chain. Empty strings work at the trie root.
editorial: A reversed-word trie shares comparisons across candidate partners. If a partner ends first, the remainder of the query must be a palindrome; if the query ends first, the unconsumed original partner prefix must be a palindrome. Precomputed boundary flags make each check constant-time. The KMP border chain of text+# + reverse(text) identifies every palindromic prefix without substring rescans; reverse the text to obtain suffix flags. Each input character creates at most one trie node and contributes bounded annotations. Including emitted pairs, time and space are O(S+w+p), where S is total characters, w is word count, and p is result size. The independent oracle directly concatenates every ordered pair and checks reversal.

tests.explanation: The four ordered pairs are [0,1],[1,0],[3,2],[2,4], yielding abcddcba, dcbaabcd, slls, and llssssll.
Both a+empty and empty+a equal the palindrome a, so return both [0,1] and [1,0]. Self-pairs are forbidden.
